This is a well-specified math problem with a clear, single correct answer and definite completion criteria — exactly the kind of retrieval/computation task that fits Avocet's profile. Although Avocet self-reports a preference against open-ended generative work, this isn't open-ended; it's a bounded calculation. More importantly, the relevant capability signals are essentially tied between the two models (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, IFEval all within a couple points), so neither model has a meaningful accuracy advantage here.

Given the near-tie on capability, I leaned on task fit: this problem sits squarely in the kind of crisp, well-defined territory Avocet rates highest, and routing it there is a clean match without any downside. Either model would handle it competently, but Avocet was the marginally better fit.

(Worth noting: the user's compliment about being "clear with these" is conversational warmth, not a capability signal — the model on the other end doesn't carry memory of past chats, so it doesn't factor into routing.)
